source.title: Scaling SGD Batch Size to 32K for ImageNet Training
source.authors: Yang You; Igor Gitman; Boris Ginsburg

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling affects the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: It compares held-out ImageNet accuracy across batch sizes and training recipes, and examines whether large-batch accuracy loss reflects a train–test loss gap.
record.gate_note: The paper reports accuracy and training–testing loss-gap results relevant to V5. Its discussion of cited studies is not recorded as results. Table 2's weight-to-gradient ratios and Figures 2–5's unquantified curves are not separate claim-version results.
record.test_reason: The study compares ImageNet held-out accuracy across batch sizes and training recipes, including fixed-duration comparisons and a longer-training sweep. These results directly test V5, including its recipe-adaptation qualification.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion. They argue that LARS addresses optimization difficulties, allowing Alexnet to reach approximately baseline accuracy at 8K and Resnet-50 at 32K. They describe longer training as completely recovering Alexnet-BN accuracy at 32K, although Table 5 reaches 59.9% versus the 60.2% reference. Their conclusion's broader statement about Alexnet scaling to 32K should be read with that distinction. Training above 32K without accuracy loss remains open.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses ImageNet classifiers and compares large-batch SGD recipes, including LARS with warm-up, rather than reproducing all settings in the cited large-batch studies. It also reports a batch-32K training-duration sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with architecture and training recipe: Alexnet versus Alexnet-BN, LARS versus the earlier larger-learning-rate recipe, batch size, warm-up, and epoch count.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report no significant change in the training–testing loss gap between batch 256 and batch 8K for Alexnet-BN, despite lower held-out accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A large-batch accuracy penalty can reflect poorer optimization without an increased training–testing loss gap.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The accuracy comparison uses limited ImageNet evaluation (one model and 1 central crop); the authors note that their Resnet-50 baseline is below published state of the art and cite differences in augmentation and testing. Figure 1 is not numerically tabulated.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization in the same architectures and training recipes.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required to interpolate.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited and broader tuning. LARS experiments do not provide this comparison at matched batch sizes.

Language models and normalization or regularization changes beyond replacing Alexnet's local response normalization with batch normalization. Section 3's BN comparison does not establish matched epoch budgets.
Controlled dropout addition, removal, strength and training-set-size effects.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

missing.what: The matched Table 1(a) small-batch Alexnet reference is 58.8% at batch 512, LR=0.02, with 2.5-epoch warm-up; R1 instead records the separate 58% Section 3 reference.

The learning-rate sweep shows recipe sensitivity and divergence: Alexnet reaches only 0.1% at batch 4096 with LR=0.07 and batch 8192 with LR=0.05; the text reports divergence above LR=0.06 despite warm-up.

For Alexnet-BN, broad LARS learning-rate intervals yield similar outcomes: approximately 59.3% at batch 16K for LRs 13–22 and approximately 57.5% at batch 32K for LRs 17–28. This shows the residual penalty is not confined to one selected learning rate.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source listed for V5. Its adaptation successes support qualifications already present in V5; its residual large-batch penalties do not contradict that version. R7 cannot support a V5 verdict about held-out accuracy. Section 3's BN epoch-budget ambiguity prevents a clean fixed-budget verdict from R4–R6. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Language models, workload-dependent batch thresholds, and comparisons at a fixed epoch budget across broad settings; the paper tests image classifiers on ImageNet.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
